§11.2.6 Log Scale Charts

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-log-scale-charts · charts types

✅ Normative

A logarithmic axis changes the reading, not the chart table. Unprinted values MUST be estimated against the printed decade bands, by the mark's position inside its band, and SHOULD be given to no more than two significant figures.

On a tenfold-per-band axis the same visual gap covers ever larger ranges, so a value is interpolated by position inside the band, not linearly: a mark a third of the way from 1 000 to 10 000 is near 2 000, not near 4 000. The tolerance a checker allows is chosen by readability like any estimate (see Values and Tolerances§11.1.4).

Event callouts naming years (1976: Tangshan Earthquake, China) are commentary: they add no row or column, and their text is kept as text (see Multiple Charts and Reference Ink§11.1.3).

✅ Sample — catastrophe-review-2025_p26

Two charts over the same 55-year axis ticked every third year: event counts on a linear axis (Figure 16) and victims on 1 000 → 10 000 000 decade bands (Figure 17). Each has its own table under its own title, both series across all 55 years — the ticked years by their printed labels, the years between by their axis values (1971, 2023). On the log chart, every value is a band-position estimate to two significant figures, written in the axis's digit grouping, except the two 2024 values, which the side text prints (11 000, 3 200): printed beats geometry, so they are copied. The event callouts and the side text follow the log chart's table as text. Only the first two and last two years of each table are shown.
